title: Tame the p99
intro: A live request queue under real traffic. Your SLA is on the tail, not the average.
briefing: Traffic just spiked to 900 req/s and the queue is drowning — watch p99 run away. Finance says you get at most 6 servers. Get p99 under 200 ms and hold it. Remember: response time = waiting + processing, and you have TWO levers.
debrief: Adding servers alone can't save you inside the budget: 6 servers × (1000/10 ms) = 600 req/s < 900 — still past the knee, so the queue (waiting time) keeps growing. The winning move is to also cut SERVICE TIME: at 6 ms, six servers absorb 1,000 req/s and the queue drains; p99 falls back toward the service time. That's the two-lever lesson — capacity handles waiting, optimisation handles processing — and notice how p99 lags after the fix while the bad tail flushes out of the window. Systems recover on percentile-time, not wall-time.
